title: Twists and shifted graded-module sheaves on a degree-one covered Proj
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring and put $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. Assume that the standard opens $D_+(f)$ for $f\in S_1$ cover $X$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbf Z}M_d$ be any graded $S$-module, with $S_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$. Use the associated sheaves and shifts $M(n)_d=M_{n+d}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], and put $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$. For all $n\in\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal O_X(n)$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], and the canonical multiplication maps $\mathcal O_X(a)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(b)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X(a+b)$ and $\alpha_{M,n}:\widetilde M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(n)\longrightarrow\widetilde{M(n)}$ are isomorphisms [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Here $a,b\in\mathbf Z$; on a chart $D_+(f)$ with $f\in S_1$, the maps send $(u/f^r)\otimes(v/f^s)$ to $uv/f^{r+s}$, using scalar multiplication when $u$ is in $M$. These multiplication maps are unital, associative, and natural in degree-preserving maps of graded modules.

source.place: Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, all three multiplication isomorphisms; Tag 01MS, lemma-when-invertible, chart formula; equations equation-multiply and equation-multiply-more-generally.

proof.text: Apply gradedModuleSheaf_exists to each shifted grading M(a), whose internal direct-sum decomposition is obtained by reindexing the original decomposition by addition of a. Chart injectivity and the specified scalar and restriction equations identify F(a) with this quasi-coherent associated sheaf. The positive homogeneous basic opens form a basis. Descend each actual twist section to its homogeneous localized fraction by twist_fraction_descent; basicOpen_localization_detection makes that fraction unique and proves its additivity, scalar equation and restriction equation.

On each positive basic open multiply the localized module fraction by the descended twist fraction. The shifted degree condition places the result in the chart range, including the zero numerator when its prospective degree is negative. Chart injectivity proves bilinearity. For an inclusion with g^e=c*f, the product of the two restrictions is c^(r+s)*(v*y)/g^(e*(r+s)), which is the restriction of the product. Lift this bilinear map to the sectionwise tensor product, extend the resulting restriction-compatible linear maps from the basis using the sheaf basis-extension equivalence, and descend through the module-sheafification adjunction. This constructs mult(a,b) with the fraction formula on every positive basic open.

source.place: Equations multiply and multiply-more-generally preceding Tag 01MS.

proof.text: Use the existing isInvertible_twist and twistTensorIso, obtained by gluing the degree-one free generators f^a. On any open inside a degree-one chart, write both input sections as scalar multiples of the free generators. The generator equation for twistTensorIso then shows that its output is their pointwise product. These chart computations cover every open and show the product formula globally. The existing unitIsoTwistZero identifies the tensor unit with twist zero.

source.place: Tag 01MS, degree-one trivializations and multiplication; Tag 01MT.

proof.text: Two maps out of a sheaf tensor agree if their composites with the sectionwise tensor-to-sheaf map agree: use the module-sheafification adjunction and tensor induction. For the iterated tensors needed here, the two right factors are twists. The source is quasi-coherent; detect equality on sections over the affine degree-one cover, and use the free generator of each twist successively to write every section as a nested pure tensor. Thus pure triples suffice without any assertion of global pure generation. Apply these detection statements, the product formula for twists and injectivity of the module charts to prove both twist unit laws, twist associativity, the module right unit law and module associativity. The equalities reduce respectively to multiplication by one and associativity or commutation of scalar multiplication.

source.place: Coherence of equations multiply and multiply-more-generally; sheafification tensor product as in Modules on Sites, Section 03EK.

proof.text: The module unit equation implies mult(a,0) is an isomorphism. Module associativity at (a,b,-b) implies that (mult(a,b) tensor O(-b)) followed by mult(a+b,-b) is an isomorphism, since b+(-b)=0 and the twist comparison is an isomorphism. Applying this to (a+b,-b) shows every mult(a,b) is epic, after transporting the integer indices. The same composite shows mult(a,b) tensor O(-b) is monic. Tensoring with O(-b) is an equivalence, with inverse tensoring with O(b), so it reflects monomorphisms. Thus mult(a,b) is both monic and epic, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category of sheaves of modules. This replaces construction and overlap gluing of a separate local inverse.

source.place: Tag 01MS and Tag 01MT; categorical consequence of their multiplication and coherence identities.

proof.text: For naturality, the source F(a) tensor O(b) is quasi-coherent. Restriction to the degree-one affine cover detects equality of morphisms from this source, and on each affine member equality is detected on sections. Since O(b) is free there on f^b, each tensor section is a pure tensor with that generator. Write the two factors as localized fractions. The assumed fraction equations for chi, beta and mult identify the two sides with phi(v*y)/f^(r+s) and v*phi(y)/f^(r+s), equal by S-linearity. No construction of a new tilde functor is required. Empty charts and zero modules are included in these universal properties.

source.place: Tag 01M7 functoriality and naturality of equation multiply-more-generally.

proof_origin.place: V6 formalization of the fraction construction of 01MS/01MT, using existing degree-one twist trivializations; categorical inversion from the proved module unit and associativity laws replaces a separately glued inverse. Tensor detection uses the sheafification adjunction; for iterated tensors the quasi-coherent source and the two free twist generators suffice.
